title: Dispatch: finding registry review corrections from PR #476 (attempt 3)
description:
HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #476 returned "changes required": three P1 findings and two
P2. All five are accepted. Read the inline comments on
https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/476 for the reviewer's exact wording.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== P1-A: QUERIES CANNOT EXPRESS EXACT MEMBERSHIP (findingRegistry.ts:569) ===
`records.filter(...)` returns only WHOLE RECORDS, but most findings are about
nested creature entries, readiness clauses, table cells, option payloads, or
exact source-backed paths. The predicates compound it by selecting broad
families: half-damage selects every creature and hazard; engine-capability
ownership selects any record with any engineHooks — rather than the audited
affected branches or the pending item clauses.

Consequence: a repaired unrelated record appears in the snapshot while an
affected nested clause is omitted, and the row has no identity capable of
detecting either. The registry's own documented contract says a broad thematic
category is not membership evidence.

Fix: return STABLE MEMBERSHIP IDENTITIES — `{ recordKey, clauseId or path,
sourceSpan }` — record-only where that genuinely is the unit. Every query must
enumerate the source-grounded affected members. Where the current pack cannot
express the needed identity (because the clause IR is not landed yet), say so
explicitly on the row with a defined follow-up rather than substituting a
thematic kind set.

=== P1-B: indep:011 IS ACCEPTED, NOT AMBIGUOUS (finding-registry.json:76) ===
*** THIS ONE IS MY FAULT, NOT YOURS. *** The attempt-2 dispatch spec told you to
mark it ambiguous, following the parent bead's wording. The review overturned
both, and the parent bead has been corrected.

The source rule permits the standard language catalog PLUS another
campaign-common language and, with GM permission, exotic/secret languages. The
pack falsely CLOSES that universe. Whether the pack must expose the extension
point is NOT ambiguous — it must. Only the chosen custom language requires
adjudication. The repair plan routes the finding to C1/C3, i.e.
eshyra-o9bd.19.3.1 and .19.3.3.

Fix: status accepted, correct owner, and a regressionForm that proves the open
escape hatch remains available.

=== P1-C: indep:001 AND sol:CAP-001 MUST NOT SHARE A ROW (json:293) ===
They name different defects:
  * indep:001 — the audit/readiness GATES treat atom presence as complete
    procedure coverage. Correction path A5/V1/V2 = eshyra-o9bd.19.1.5,
    .19.6.1, .19.6.2.
  * sol:CAP-001 — the 335-record rule CORPUS lacks executable procedures.
    Correction path C4/E0/E11 = eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4, .19.5.1, .19.5.12.
Either can recur after the other is fixed. Split into separate canonical rows,
memberships, owners and regression forms so closing one cannot silently close
the other.

While you are there: re-check the other multi-alias rows against this same test —
"could one of these recur while the other is fixed?" — and split any that fail
it. There are only three multi-alias rows left, so this is quick.

=== P2-D: DUPLICATE canonicalId IS NOT DETECTED (findingRegistry.ts:276) ===
`aliases.has(row.canonicalId)` checks the ALIAS map, which contains alias keys,
so it stays false even when two rows share a canonicalId. Keep a separate Set of
canonical IDs and check it before inserting each row. Add a mutation test that
duplicates a canonicalId and asserts rejection.

=== P2-E: THE MEMBERSHIP TEST PERMITS 66 EMPTY QUERIES (test:95) ===
It asserts only that SOME query returns a non-empty result, so a typo, a renamed
record, or source drift can silently vacate an individual finding while CI stays
green.

Fix: assert expected stable member identities per row, or commit a GENERATED
membership snapshot and diff against it. Every accepted or narrowed finding that
should have corpus membership must be non-empty. Rows that legitimately have
zero members (policy/adjudication rows) must be explicitly marked and justified
so they are distinguishable from accidental emptiness rather than passing
incidentally.

NOTE ON COUNT HYGIENE: a committed snapshot of generated member IDENTITIES is
NOT a hand-copied count and does not violate the count-hygiene rule. What is
forbidden is a human transcribing a total (391, 399, 77, 79) into an assertion.
A regenerable snapshot of identities is exactly the right instrument here.

=== UNCHANGED ===
All 70 aliases still resolve to exactly one canonical row each. No hand-copied
totals. Qualified prefixes only. sol:CAP-002 stays NARROWED with the
no-regression requirement on existing typed condition effects. Records use the
`key` field, not `id`; executionReadiness is at
`record.data.executionReadiness`.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
This worktree already contains the previous attempts' committed work; you are
correcting it, not starting over. Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under FILES YOU OWN. A sibling dispatch is running
  in parallel on a disjoint file set. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete an existing test to make a finding go away. If
  an existing test encodes the defective behavior, CHANGE it deliberately and
  say so in your completion notes with the reason.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.
acceptance_criteria:
• Every membership query returns stable member identities (recordKey plus clause/path/span where the unit is nested), enumerating source-grounded affected members.
• Rows whose exact identity cannot yet be expressed say so explicitly with a defined follow-up, rather than substituting a thematic kind set.
• indep:011 is accepted, correctly owned, with a regression proving the open language escape hatch.
• indep:001 and sol:CAP-001 are separate rows with separate owners, memberships and regression forms; other multi-alias rows re-checked against the same test.
• Duplicate canonicalId is rejected, proven by a mutation test.
• Per-row membership is asserted against expected identities or a generated snapshot; legitimate zero-member rows are explicitly marked and justified.
• All 70 aliases still resolve to exactly one canonical row.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
